title: Load a flat steak knife into a dishwasher's lidded cutlery basket: turn it upright, lower it through a 24 mm opening
instruction: Put the steak knife from the cutting board into the dishwasher's cutlery basket, then take your hands away.
context: Most homes load a dishwasher's cutlery basket every day, and whoever unloads it reaches in by hand, often a child doing chores. Bosch's manual (SPX68B55UC): 'Load knives and other sharp utensils with their handles up to reduce the risk of cut-type injuries.' CPSC's emergency-room sample (NEISS, 2019-2023) has 183 cases naming a knife in a dishwasher, about 7,700 visits nationally; 18 say the knife was up, e.g. 'A KNIFE WAS STICKING STRAIGHT UP AND CUT HER ARM'. The 220 mm knife (110 mm blade) goes from flat on the board to within about 25 degrees of upright to pass a 24 mm-wide lid opening, then down into a 125 mm-deep cell until its handle stands at most 95 mm above the lid.
setup: Positions from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the left arm), heights above the bench top. Open dishwasher door: its inner panel (stainless; a 20 mm board in a real trial), 500 x 460 mm, flat, centred at (0.36, -0.08), with two rack rails. Lower rack on it (white nylon-coated steel wire): 420 x 420 mm (x 0.14-0.56, y -0.29-0.13), floor 32 mm up, side walls 100 mm high; plate tines at the back holding two 260 mm dinner plates. Cutlery basket (grey polypropylene) in the rack's front left: 120 x 180 x 131 mm (x 0.20-0.32, y -0.07-0.11), six 60 mm square cells in two rows of three under a fixed grid lid, top 163 mm up (cells 125 mm deep from floor to lid underside); over each cell one 42 x 24 mm opening (long side along y, centred 13 mm nearer the robot than the cell's centre; in a real trial the openings are the named basket's own, fit-checked against these sizes). Already in it: a fork tines up (back left cell), a spoon bowl up (front left), a spoon bowl down (back right), each standing in its cell's opening. On the bench: a wooden cutting board, 300 x 200 x 15 mm, centred at (0.245, 0.30). On it, lying flat: an Arcos Monoblock steak knife 375500 (one-piece stainless, serrated, dishwasher safe; 220 mm overall, 110 mm blade from heel to point; in the sim the handle is 20 mm wide and 14 mm thick and the blade 16 mm wide and 2 mm thick, estimates; 75 g), along x at y 0.32, its point towards the robot at x 0.138, its butt at x 0.358. Fit-check: the cells must be at least 125 mm deep from floor to lid underside for this knife.
scoring: Judged at the end, everything still for 1 s, from top and side photos, a protractor, a ruler and the trial video. 'Point up' means the point is above the handle with the knife more than 20 degrees from level. 0 if: at any time the knife is let go point up over the rack, or comes to rest point up in the rack or basket; or it falls off the bench (dropped on the bench or board and picked up again is fine); or at the end a gripper is within 5 cm of it. Otherwise: 1.0 when the knife is released, point down in one cell, within 20 degrees of upright (protractor on the side photo), with the handle's end at most 95 mm above the lid's top face (ruler), the point and the handle's end over the same cell; 0.25 when point down in a cell but not meeting that (caught or hung in the opening), or lying on the lid, point not up; 0 anywhere else.
reset_notes: Lift the knife out of the basket by its handle, straight up, and lay it back flat on the board in its taped outline, point towards the robot. Nothing is consumed; the cutlery already in the basket stays. For operator safety on the shared rig the knife's edge is dulled and its tip rounded to about 1 mm radius (still visibly pointed); keep a cork on the point between trials.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz; all parts rigid, built from boxes; the tip is a 4 mm-wide step (the real tip is rounded to ~1 mm radius); the knife's handle and blade cross-sections are estimates. Knife friction 0.9 (estimate). The lid is fixed (real lids hinge); the cutlery already in the basket is fixed. Fit-check the real basket's cell depth (sim 125 mm) and openings. Real trial: the Arcos 375500, edge dulled, tip rounded.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers closed early and hovered 17-28 cm up, the left drifting back from over the knife; nothing was touched). Scripted demo: 1.0 (knife seated in the front middle cell, 4 degrees from upright, handle end 92 mm above the lid, edge heel 15 mm below it; step 330).
